feature: Edit Last Capture from the menu bar
summary: Once the capture toast has faded, one keystroke (Shift-Command-6) or one menu item opens your newest capture in an editor. The menu bar menu no longer lists a Preferences item that did nothing.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. No flags: this is shared shell code, so Current has it too.

try.do: Press Shift-Command-4 and capture any region. Wait for the toast to fade.
Press Shift-Command-6 from any app. The capture opens in a Photonz editor window.
Close that window. Open the menu bar icon and pick Edit Last Capture. The same capture opens again.
With an editor window frontmost, open the Capture menu in the menu bar. Edit Last Capture is listed there with the same shortcut.
Record a short clip with Shift-Command-5, stop it, then press Shift-Command-6. The video editor opens instead of the image editor.
Open the menu bar menu and look at the bottom group. Preferences is gone; every item there does something.

evaluate: Does Shift-Command-6 feel like the natural next number after 3, 4 and 5, or would you have reached for another chord?
After a capture, is the hotkey fast enough that you stop waiting on the toast at all?
Is Edit Last Capture in the right spot in the menu, next to Show History, or does it belong with the capture commands above the divider?
Do you miss the Preferences item as a hint that settings are coming, or is the shorter menu better?
rough: Edit Last Capture opens whatever history lists first. That is the newest file in your Screenshots folder, so a file you drop there by hand counts as the last capture.

On a Mac with a Touch Bar, Shift-Command-6 is the system's Touch Bar screenshot shortcut and will intercept ours until it is turned off in System Settings, the same way Shift-Command-3 and 4 do. The Welcome window's shortcut check does not mention it yet; filed as a follow-up.

This session could not press the hotkey or open the live menu itself (the unmanned terminal has neither Accessibility nor Automation permission), so the build, the test suite and a code walk are the verification. The steps above are the real check.
The two menus still name the region capture differently (Capture Region in the menu bar, Capture Rectangle in the Capture menu). Pre-existing; filed as a follow-up.
